issues: Timeline row pill for kind label (INTELLIGENCE_APPROVED) visually overlaps the severity text (`MAJOR` / `MODERATE`) at 1920 width — the summary cell text collides with the fixed-width kind pill. Purely cosmetic; both are readable but overlap visually.

React hydration warning: `<span> cannot be a child of <option>`. Non-blocking; caused by option content wrapping. Recommend inspecting <option> renders (likely a select in properties/missions dropdown) and using plain text instead of <span> children.
Two 404 asset fetches persist on /ceo/login (carried over from iter23) — non-blocking.

action_items: Optional cosmetic: fix timeline row overlap between kind pill and summary text on Passport page (grid `140px 160px 1fr` collapses the pill width on some entries).
Optional cosmetic: replace <span> child of <option> in one of the select renders to silence React hydration warning.
critical_code_review_comments: intelligence.py review handler updates the PIO twice on approve (first sets state=approved+increments version, then re-updates state=passport_committed). Consider a single atomic write to avoid a transient `approved` state that could be observed by a concurrent reader between the two updates.

intelligence.py `_content_hash(pio_content)` hashes only user-submitted body — not the tenant/property/mission binding. Approved intelligence hashes therefore aren't stable-per-tenant, but this may be intentional (the Passport entry hash chains everything). Confirm.

passport_service.py `_next_seq()` uses `find_one_and_update` with `return_document=True` — motor accepts booleans, but PyMongo docs strongly recommend `pymongo.ReturnDocument.AFTER`. Works today; will silently break if pymongo tightens the type check.

passport_service.py `_ensure_passport` inserts a sequence with `next_seq=1`, then `_next_seq` `$inc:1` returns `next_seq-1=1`. Therefore the GENESIS entry has `seq=1` (not `seq=0`). Not a bug (GENESIS is identified by `prior_hash=null`) but the seq numbering may surprise ledger consumers expecting 0-based indices.

passport_service.py `read_passport_projection` treats `contractor/adjuster/insurer` as always-visible regardless of the entry's visibility payload. If ever a PIO explicitly sets `visibility.contractor=false`, this projection will still expose it to contractor audience.

intelligence.py `_project_intelligence_for_report` filter: `p.get('visibility', {}).get(tmpl['visibility'], False) or tmpl['visibility'] == 'internal'` — this correctly maps `executive_summary` (internal audience) to all PIOs, but `hoa_summary` uses audience 'public' which will filter to only PIOs with `visibility.public=true`. Homeowners could hit an empty HOA report; product should confirm this matches intent.

intelligence.py `create_intelligence` — after Pydantic validates enums via defaults, the `_validate_enums` manual check is redundant (Pydantic already coerces to strings). It still fires because the model accepts any string. Consider using `Literal[...]` types in the schema to reject at the 422 layer for consistency with FastAPI docs.
intelligence.py evidence tenant check uses `mission_id: body.mission_id` in the find query; this is correct and prevents cross-mission evidence reuse even within the same tenant — good.
